text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
AL-RAI
- Jordan and Egypt to sign six protocols and agreements today during visit to Cairo by Prime Minister Abdul-Salam al-Majali.
- Foreign Minister Fayez al-Tarawnah says Jordan will participate in Middle East economic summit.

- Military prosecutors at trial of Jordanian soldier accused of killing seven Israelis push for guilty verdict on charges of premeditated murder, planning to kill, threatening with a weapon, and military disobedience.
AD-DUSTOUR
- 55,000 tonnes of French wheat arrives in Jordan's Red Sea port of Aqaba, bound for Iraq under the oil-for-food programme.
- Israeli plan to assassinate PLO's Abu Mazen foiled.
- Plans to set up a Christian Democrat party in Jordan stirs up anger. Formal application to be made to Interior Ministry within a week.
AL ARAB AL YAWM
- Majali says in Cairo that Jordan supports setting up Arab free trade zone.
- Jordan seeks 30 million Ecu ($36 million) loan from European Investment Bank to help finance expansion plans in Aqaba.
- Police fire tear gas in east Amman to prevent clashes between youths. 50 arrested and one policeman injured.
AL-ASWAQ
- Local branches of Islamic Action Front have presented 30 names as IAF candidates in parliamentary elections.
- Head of Jordan's insurance firms association says insurance companies to be given extra time to raise their capital to 2 million dinars.
JORDAN TIMES
- Israel proposes joint Israeli-Jordanian airport at Aqaba be run by an independent firm. Jordan says study must be done on the proposal.
- International Moslem Brotherhood sends arbitrator to help resolve differences amongst Jordan's Islamists.
- Information Minister Samir Mutawae says Jordan will not allow anti-Israeli signs on shops and properties.
